source: Native cached georeferenced OS London five-foot 1893 map; no Goad coverage claimed
method: Restore mapped depot fan throats and exact running-track connection. Upstream eleven stems retain reviewed source routes, while final paired stem tips converge onto common mapped switch nodes. Height and formation construction are explicitly interpreted.

branchJoin.evidence: Join the western running track using the existing first branch segment normal and +1.8 m centre offset. The shared box helper uses y as bottom: ordinary branch rails begin at formation+0.33 m and have 0.13 m depth, hence rail top is formation+0.46 m. The detailed branch uses the same+0.46 m rail-top datum. This renderer datum is not a surveyed historic rail level.

profile.evidence: The OS fixes plan geometry and has local benchmarks around 14–18 ft, but does not establish this model grade. Hold existing branch formation of 5.5 m over a shared level approach derived from all siding intersections with both the ordinary and northern-connection branch banks, including sleeper width and a full station margin. This prevents rails disappearing below the existing bank/ballast. Keep a long linear 240 m transition farther outward, resolving the inherited level difference at about 1:44. Equal graph distance gives shared junctions identical formation and rail-top levels. These levels and earth slopes are explicit model interpretations, not an original railway gradient.

junctionTreatment.method: Retain every upstream source control; curve only within the final 14 m approach, followed by 4 m exactly along the receiving track tangent. Shared node plan centre, both gauge rail endpoints and formation/rail-top levels therefore coincide. These short turnout curves interpret the mapped converging fan; no surveyed switch specification is asserted.
